sections.content: How many people are "production managers and directors in manufacturing"?

280,105 people

were counted on the census as "production managers and directors in manufacturing" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Production managers and directors in manufacturing organise and direct the activities and resources necessary for production in manufacturing industries including the maintenance of engineering items, equipment and machinery.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "production managers and directors in manufacturing" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "production managers and directors in manufacturing", 16.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "production managers and directors in manufacturing" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "production managers and directors in manufacturing" included:

  • production managers and directors in construction
  • chief executives and senior officials
  • complementary health associate professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "production managers and directors in manufacturing" there were more men than women (78.9% compared with 21.1%).

This means "production managers and directors in manufacturing" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "corporate managers and directors".

Men made up 78.9% and women made up 21.1% of "production managers and directors in manufacturing"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "production managers and directors in manufacturing" included:

  • production and process engineers
  • chemical and related process operatives
  • caretakers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "production managers and directors in manufacturing" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "production managers and directors in manufacturing" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "production managers and directors in manufacturing", 7.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (87.2% compared with 12.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (81.1%) than self-employed (18.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Buckinghamshire, this is in the same region of the South East.
